### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s).

**35** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 560b724c957f38f618a11d59d926fcb8fc1c0fb2`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 560b724c957f38f618a11d59d926fcb8fc1c0fb2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c23d77a589e9bd43dd1df302f81c8eeb7a31e3da` — the merge of head `8d314ac6760b1240cee680c874b2830010cf7aa1` into base `560b724c957f38f618a11d59d926fcb8fc1c0fb2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c23d77a589e9bd43dd1df302f81c8eeb7a31e3da && git checkout c23d77a589e9bd43dd1df302f81c8eeb7a31e3da
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 560b724c957f38f618a11d59d926fcb8fc1c0fb2 8d314ac6760b1240cee680c874b2830010cf7aa1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 560b724c957f38f618a11d59d926fcb8fc1c0fb2 && git merge --no-ff 8d314ac6760b1240cee680c874b2830010cf7aa1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 560b724c957f38f618a11d59d926fcb8fc1c0fb2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 560b724c957f38f618a11d59d926fcb8fc1c0fb2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ace7e1df2e4ed8472984c36f324da6e9595ea562`

### ① Derived judgments

- **Route table enumerated at the head** (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, every `path: \`${metaPath}/:type/:name…\``): GET `/references` (7160), GET `/layers` (7323), GET plain read with the `?layers=` branch (7452), PUT/DELETE `/:type/:name` (8009/8265, writes), GET `/history` (8430), GET `/audit` (8586), POST `/publish` (8722), POST `/rollback` (8923), GET `/diff` (9041), GET `/published` (9359). Two literal-typed siblings sit beside them: GET `/book/:name/tree` (7374) and GET `/object/:name/state/:field` (9225). Every content-serving `/:type/:name/*` GET now either calls `metaItemReadGate` (`/layers`, `?layers=true` via `serveMetaItemLayered`; `/published` via `servePublished`; `/diff` inline; `/history` and `/audit` via `eventDoorRefusal`) or carries a stated exemption (`/references`). The `/references` exemption is **correct**: `findReferencesToMeta` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:22457`) answers `{ references: [{ type, name, label }] }` of other items, no member of this item's document. `/book/:name/tree` is outside the `/:type/:name` spelling but already carries its own §6.7 gate through the same `resolveDocsAudience` (`admitsBook` + `readableTree`), so no door is missed. **Correct.**
- **One gate, one resolver.** `metaItemReadGate` (head 3834-4162) is the single function; the plain read (7869-7877), `serveMetaItemLayered` (4776), `/published` (9384), `/diff` (9109) and `eventDoorRefusal` (4004) all call it; no per-door copy exists. The doc/book arms call the existing `resolveDocsAudience` / `fetchAudienceBooks` / `readDocCorpus`; the app arm calls the existing `filterAppForUserWithReason` + `resolveNavDocAudience`. No second audience resolver, consistent with ruling 5793362670 item 1. **Correct.**
- **Per-door × per-type answer.** `/published` runs `arms: 'all', partial: 'prune'` and answers byte-for-byte the plain read's arms (doc/book refusal, app 403/404/pruned, dashboard widget gate, object mask via `maskObjectDocument`). `/layers`, `?layers=true`, `/diff` run `arms: 'per-caller', partial: 'refuse'`: doc/book refuse where the plain read refuses; app refuses 403 where the plain read refuses, and 403 where it would prune; object masked as the plain read (`applyObjectSchemaMask` projects only `fields`, `packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.ts`, so the `/diff` fields-only projection is exactly the plain read's). `diffMetaItem` is `diffShallow`, top-level (`protocol.ts:3945`, comment at 21385), so `diffSides` and the `path === 'fields'` match are sound. No door serves more than the plain read to any caller. **Correct.**
- **Dropped per-deployment arms verified at source.** `filterDashboardForUser` reads only a `serviceGate` built by `resolveRegisteredServices` (kernel `getServiceAsync` probe); `requiresService` on app entries is the same probe; ADR-0057 D10 PS-2 note: "nav lives and dies with the capability", registered per deployment. Neither reads the caller. The `servability` arm derives from object `enable` (deployment). Calling them per-deployment is **correct**; dropping them on stored-version doors withholds nothing from any caller.
- **Anonymous callers.** The `/meta` umbrella gate (`registerMetadataEndpoints`, 6074-6122, `registerPerItemRoute` reads `this.routeManager` at call time so it is inside) 401s every meta route for a caller with no `userId` (`shouldDenyAnonymous`, `packages/core/src/security/anonymous-deny.ts`) except `isPublicAudienceRead`: GET `/meta/:type` and `/meta/:type/:name` for book/doc and `/book/:name/tree`. So `?layers=true` was the one anonymously reachable alternate door, and it ran before any audience gate; now the doc/book arm's `docsAudienceRefusal` answers 401. A public doc stays readable via `?layers=true` (docReader → `docAudienceAllows` public). **Correct.**
- **Census fails without the fix, and reads the live route table.** Ran in a throwaway worktree: head → 194/194 green; with `main`'s `rest-server.ts` swapped in → 38 red (35 census cells matching the PR's red list plus the 3 edge pins). Registering an undeclared `GET /:type/:name/mutant` reddens exactly the route-table row (`rest.getRoutes()` filtered on `itemPath` prefix). Real, not hard-coded; scoped to the `/:type/:name` spelling only (a literal-typed door such as `/meta/app/:name/foo` would escape it). Full rest suite at head: 197 files, 3518 passed, 1 skipped, exit 0, matching the PR's numbers.
- **`content/docs/ui/apps.mdx` paragraph** (358-367): every sentence matches the code (`/published` serves the filtered body; `/layers` and `/diff` refuse 403 on a partly-withheld app; `requiresService` entries served as stored). True. No other doc page states anything false; `adding-a-metadata-type.mdx:180` still truthfully says the wrapper loads `?layers=true`.
- **Changeset.** Every "before" sentence is true at `main` (`/published` did `res.json(layered.overlay)` / `res.json(data)` ungated; `/diff` did `res.json(result)`; `/history`, `/audit` had no gate). One sentence is **false**: "Types no per-caller gate judges (`view`, `flow`, and others) are untouched on every door" — `dashboard` is such a type and its `/published` door changed (the ADR-0057 D10 widget gate is newly applied there; the PR's own red list names the `dashboard` × `/published` cell and the census asserts `widgetIds(served) === ['w_open_cases']`).
- **Runtime dispatcher untouched and ungated:** `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts` at head carries no `audience`, `filterApp`, `requiredPermissions` or `permissionSet` symbol, only the ADR-0106 object mask; `git diff` on it is empty. Confirms open question 2's measurement.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` with `@objectstack/rest` `patch` is **correct; no `(narrowing)` arm is owed.** The arm (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`) exists for a diff that narrows a **published accept set** (the #16296 value-domain case). This diff removes no spec key, export, config field or accepted value; it changes which caller a read answers, which `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/execution-duties.md` line 98 places outside clause ② as the runtime permission/security class, and line 99 says pulling behaviour back to the declared contract (ADR-0046 §6.7 "gating enforced at the read layer"; apps.mdx "the entry is never served") does not touch it. Precedent: ruling 5793362670 on #19790 recorded `Clause-②: no` for "a permission-boundary tightening, no spec key". A bug fix in a released package takes `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3). The refuse-on-partial arm is a new boundary rather than a pull-back, but that is a governance question for ③, not an accept-set narrowing.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1 (refuse instead of prune on stored-version app doors).** Within the card's closure rule by its letter ("answers what the plain read answers, or refuses"). It **does** create a new permission boundary: no prior contract said the layered view or diff requires every entry permission; the PR writes that sentence into apps.mdx itself, and triage (5852543510, carried from 5830552645) reserved a refusal boundary to the maintainer, with the claim stating such a route "stops the dev at `needs_decision`"; the dev shipped it and posed the question instead. It **does** lock out legitimate Studio editors: `filterAppForUserWithReason` has no admin exemption (`sysPerms.has(p)` exact), and a platform admin's `systemPermissions` is the fixed seven-item `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES` list (`packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts`: `manage_users`, `manage_metadata`, `manage_platform_settings`, `manage_sharing`, `setup.access`, `setup.write`, `studio.access`, no wildcard). Probed in the worktree with exactly that list against an app carrying `requiredPermissions: ['finance.access']`: plain read 200 pruned; `?layers=true` and `/layers` 403 PERMISSION_DENIED. A platform admin therefore cannot open Studio's `DesignerEditorWrapper` (documented to load `?layers=true`) or `/diff` for any app with an app-authored entry permission or a doc entry gated to a set they lack. The cost is stated honestly in the PR body and changeset ("hold every permission its entries require"), but neither says platform admins are included. The PR does not create a new error code.
- **Open question 2 (runtime dispatcher `/meta` ungated).** Confirmed at source: `handleMetadataRequest` applies only the ADR-0106 mask on its two-segment item branch and `/published` branch; no per-caller gate on the plain read either. Leaving it to a separate card is correct: it is a transport with no gate, not a door skipping one, and a port into `runtime` would be the second resolver ruling 5793362670 item 1 forbids; the seat owes the card.
- **CI on the head is RED.** Check-runs at `ace7e1df`: 32 success, 2 skipped, 1 failure: `Lint & Repo Gates`, step 189 "Issue citations this change adds resolve on the board", exit 2 (findings). Replicated: of the 12 distinct `#N` the diff adds, `#6241` (added at `rest-server.ts` "[#6241] Judged on the NORMALIZED `metaType`") and `#10340` (added in `fetchCurrentMetaDocument` "[#10340] FOLDED, not raw") return 404 from the issues API; both are already cited on `main` (8 and 13 times) but the gate is diff-scoped by design. Tier S landing requires every check green.
- **Census net is spelling-scoped.** The route-table row catches only `/:type/:name…` registrations; literal-typed doors (`/book/:name/tree`, `/object/:name/state/:field`, or a future `/meta/app/:name/x`) fall outside it. Not a defect today (both existing ones are outside the class), but the "a door added later fails" claim should be read with that limit.
- **Minor, disclosed and acceptable:** `/diff` of a doc/book/app with no current document now answers 404 (the plain read's answer); a gate-input store fault on `/layers`/`/diff` now answers the fault (503) rather than the body; a book whose historical version carried a stricter audience now refuses the non-holder's diff of it. `/references` remains ungated by design and is outside this card.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20156-alternate-door-read-gates`
Reviewed-by: `session_01UYBdGBzWSrAMzpW8ah3GbP`

Independence: INDEPENDENT AGENT (fed the cards, the rulings and the PR only; not the dispatch order or the seat's conclusions)

**VERDICT: FAIL**
- Make `Lint & Repo Gates` green: rewrite the two added citations `#6241` and `#10340` per the gate's remedy (name a target that resolves, or keep the number and say in prose that it no longer resolves and what the live record is).
- The refuse-on-partial boundary on `/layers`, `?layers=true` and `/diff` for apps needs the maintainer's ruling on open question 1 (A / B / C) recorded on the card before this PR lands; a seat's contract review cannot supply that word, and the PR must not be readied, queued or auto-merged until it exists. Whichever option is ruled, the changeset and apps.mdx must state that platform admins are not exempt (or that they are, if B is ruled).
- Correct the changeset sentence "Types no per-caller gate judges (`view`, `flow`, and others) are untouched on every door": `dashboard`'s `/published` door now applies the ADR-0057 D10 widget gate, and the changeset must say so.
